summary: The Veterans’ Assuring Critical Care Expansions to Support Servicemembers (ACCESS) Act of 2025 modifies the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) health care programs, focusing primarily on the Veterans Community Care Program (VCCP) and mental health residential treatment programs. The bill codifies access standards for non-VA care, introduces strict timelines for notification and appointment processing, establishes standardized screening and placement procedures for mental health and substance abuse treatment, and mandates new online tools, pilot programs, and reporting requirements.

affected_groups.effect: Receive codified standards for community care eligibility, faster notification timelines regarding care approvals and denials, new online management tools, streamlined mental health screening and placement, and expanded options for community-based care.
Benefit from an extended one-year deadline to submit claims for payment under the prompt payment standard.
affected_groups.group: VCCP Health Care Providers and Entities

affected_groups.effect: Required to implement new screening processes, tracking metrics, reporting duties, online modules, and staff training related to community care and mental health residential programs.

key_provisions: Establishes statutory access standards for non-VA community care based on drive times (30 minutes for primary care/mental health, 60 minutes for specialty care) and appointment wait times (20 days for primary care, 28 days for specialty care).
Requires the VA to notify veterans in writing within two business days regarding their eligibility for community care or the denial of a care request, including appeal instructions.
Extends the claims submission deadline for health care entities and providers under the VCCP prompt payment standard from 180 days to one year.
Mandates a standardized screening process within one year to determine veteran eligibility for priority or routine admission to mental health residential rehabilitation treatment programs.
Requires the VA to offer non-Department care options if a veteran eligible for priority mental health admission cannot be placed in a VA facility within required timeframes.
Directs the creation of an interactive online self-service module for veterans to request appointments, track referrals, and appeal care decisions.

Establishes a three-year pilot program allowing certain enrolled veterans to access outpatient mental health and substance use services through specified community providers without prior referral or pre-authorization.
missing_information: Total cost or specific appropriations required to implement the bill's provisions.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Veterans’ Assuring Critical Care Expansions to Support Servicemembers (ACCESS) Act of 2025 modifies the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) health care programs, focusing primarily on the Veterans Community Care Program (VCCP) and mental health residential treatment programs. The bill codifies access standards for non-VA care, introduces strict timelines for notification and appointment processing, establishes standardized screening and placement procedures for mental health and substance abuse treatment, and mandates new online tools, pilot programs, and reporting requirements.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation alters administrative operations and oversight within the VA health care system, specifically changing how veterans access, appeal, and track community care and specialized mental health services. It introduces mandatory performance tracking, statutory wait-time rules, and pilot programs intended to alter service delivery across both internal VA facilities and contracted community providers.
